gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-traditional-nus: Broad-nibbed pen strokes that never curl shut give this body a friendly, filled-in look on the line. Noto Traditional Nushu keeps a longer passage moving easily, while Tilt Neon's drafting-pen outline holds the top with one constant nib width.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-numans: Commanding tube-like strokes sit over a body whose tracking is pushed well past normal and whose s hangs its ends far from the spine. Numans brings the modern, sparse air.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-onest: A splayed c terminal gives Tilt Neon its signature. Onest follows in a gentle monotone of line thickness, with short ascenders above big bowls, so a longer passage glides along without ink pooling where curves turn.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-open-sans: Fineliner-flat, tube-bright and loud. Open Sans takes over below with bulky lowercase proportions and smooth curves that never clog, so a longer passage stays easy going after the heading's big display swagger.

gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-oxygen: Curves that never close back on themselves, and lowercase nearly matching the capitals, make this body feel open and contemporary. Oxygen and Tilt Neon's thick-arched n meet in one tidy rhythm.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-parkinsans: Tilt Neon draws a large x-height and short ascenders in a tube-like stroke, bold and commanding. Parkinsans steps in beneath with one stroke thickness everywhere, wide-mouthed letters that stay crisp when shrunk and lowercase rising close to capitals.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-pathway-extreme: A single-weight line, like a plotter pen draws, is the first thing Tilt Neon shows. And Pathway Extreme sits beside it with stubby ascenders and descenders around a big x-height, modern and clean against the heading's splayed c.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-preahvihear: Preahvihear has an open letter mouth like a pried oyster shell and a lofty x-height. Preahvihear keeps a longer passage easy to follow, while Tilt Neon's curves, as thick as its straight stems, hold the heading firmly.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-prompt: Prompt gives small letters an oversized look and open apertures that are easily readable. And Tilt Neon does the opposite job, skimming along on a stroke weight that never changes, bold and commanding where Prompt stays approachable.
